# The full emission spectrum {#sec-spec}

```{=html}
<div class="qd-widget" data-widget="spec" data-spec="W30_late_ext_nlte" data-compare="star_t0" data-view="full"></div>
```

The figure shows the emergent spectrum of the non-LTE solution: the continuum, with 23 hydrogen lines computed one by
one and multiplied onto it. For comparison, the TITAN star before any infall is shown (continuum only). From the far UV to
the near infrared, each feature has a definite origin.

## The continuum

| band | star without infall | with infall, non-LTE | origin of the difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| far UV 912–2000 Å [erg s⁻¹] | $1.18\times10^{43}$ | $5.8\times10^{42}$ | absorbed in the infall (Lyman-line pumping, photoionization from $n=2$) |
| optical 3646–7000 Å | $6.2\times10^{43}$ | $7.1\times10^{43}$ | not separated: the irradiated photosphere, and re-emission in the infall |
| Balmer jump [dex] | 0.23 | 0.74 | photoionization from $n=2$ in the infall |
| X 2–10 keV | — | $3.3\times10^{40}$ | the shock, through the infall |
| X 10–40 keV | — | $1.4\times10^{40}$ | the shock, through the infall |

: Band luminosities of the TITAN star at $t = 0$ (`star_t0`) and of the fed star at $4.18\times10^8$ s with
non-LTE hydrogen (`W30_late_ext_nlte`) **[computed]**. {#tbl-spec-bands}

**The photosphere** ($T_{\rm eff} = 7310$ K) makes almost all of the light. Above the Balmer edge its spectrum is
within a factor 1.2 of a blackbody at $T_{\rm eff}$. Below the edge it has a far-UV excess: 13 times the blackbody at
1500 Å, 78 times at Lyα, 770 times at 1000 Å. Between the Lyman and Balmer edges a zero-metallicity photosphere has
little continuum opacity, so the light there comes from deeper, hotter layers. Our opacities contain no lines, so this
excess is probably overestimated **[computed; interpretation]**. It powers the ionization of the infall (@sec-sm).

**The Balmer jump** grows from 0.23 dex for the bare star to 0.74 dex. The infall absorbs Balmer-continuum light in
photoionizations from $n = 2$, the very process that keeps it ionized. In LTE, with neutral, Boltzmann-populated gas,
the jump is 0.61 dex **[computed]**. A strong Balmer break here is a sign of dense gas around the star with a
populated $n=2$, not of an old stellar population **[interpretation]**.

**Electron scattering.** The Thomson depth of 5.4 does not change the continuum's shape, because the scattering is
coherent and grey. It traps the light (@sec-sm) and lengthens the photons' path, which strengthens every absorption
in the infall.

**X-rays.** The shock heats the post-shock gas to $3.7\times10^7$ K, and $\tfrac12\dot M v^2 = 2.6\times10^{42}$ erg
s$^{-1}$ is radiated as free–free emission, $7.3\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ of it above 2 keV. Only $4.7\times10^{40}$
erg s$^{-1}$ escapes above 2 keV, through a column of $9\times10^{24}$ cm$^{-2}$ that is Thomson-thick and partly
neutral. Nothing escapes below about 2 keV **[computed]**. Helium, held in LTE and therefore neutral, sets that
cut-off. If the star's far UV ionized helium as well, it could move. That is not computed. The ratio
$L_{2-10\,\rm keV}/L \approx 2\times10^{-4}$ makes this an X-ray-weak source.

## The hydrogen lines

| series | line | λ [Å] | peak / continuum | EW [Å] | $L$ [erg s⁻¹] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lyman | Lyα | 1215.7 | 64 | −99 | $4.9\times10^{41}$ |
| | Lyβ | 1025.7 | 1.8 | −1.3 | $5\times10^{39}$ |
| | Lyγ–Lyε | 973–938 | 1.1–1.2 | +0.8 to +1.5 | net absorption |
| Balmer | Hα | 6564.7 | 86 | −805 | $9.0\times10^{42}$ |
| | Hβ | 4862.7 | 8.2 | −73 | $1.70\times10^{42}$ |
| | Hγ | 4341.7 | 2.8 | −18 | $5.4\times10^{41}$ |
| | Hδ | 4102.9 | 1.6 | −4.6 | $1.6\times10^{41}$ |
| | Hε–Hθ | 3971–3799 | 1.06–1.3 | +0.8 to +5.1 | net absorption |
| Paschen | Paα | 18756 | 111 | −3160 | $1.69\times10^{42}$ |
| | Paβ | 12822 | 23 | −559 | $1.06\times10^{42}$ |
| | Paγ–Paζ | 10941–9232 | 2.3–8.9 | −205 to −35 | $(1.8$–$6.1)\times10^{41}$ |
| Brackett | Brα | 40523 | 100 | −7050 | $3.0\times10^{41}$ |
| | Brβ–Brδ | 26259–19451 | 6.0–28 | −1810 to −324 | $(1.6$–$3.0)\times10^{41}$ |

: The hydrogen lines of the fed quasi-star (vacuum wavelengths; EW < 0 is emission; $L$ = −EW × the continuum
$L_\lambda$ at the line). Each line is integrated along rays through the infall with the non-LTE populations, as one
line at a time **[computed]**. {#tbl-spec-lines}

**Why Hα is so strong.** In the outer infall the populations of $n=2$ and $n=3$ are set by the star's far UV, not
by the cold gas. The Hα source function there is 10–60 times the local continuum. The line is optically thick
everywhere (Sobolev depth 10–2800), so its luminosity is the thick-line integral $\propto\int r\,v\,S_L\,dr$
(@sec-sm-halpha). The line luminosity is starlight, absorbed in the Balmer and Paschen continua and re-emitted. It is
not recombination radiation powered by the accretion. The shock's X-rays could drive at most a few
$10^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$ of Hα through the ionizations they make **[estimate]**.

**Why it is narrow.** Half of the power comes from beyond $12R$, where the gas falls at less than about 500 km s$^{-1}$. The
FWHM is 360 km s$^{-1}$. The wings reach −1100 and +1700 km s$^{-1}$: the red wing comes from the gas falling onto the
near side of the star at up to 1770 km s$^{-1}$ **[computed; interpretation]**. Our profiles leave out electron
scattering in the line, and with $\tau_{\rm es} \approx 5$ that would broaden the wings. That is the most important
omission for comparing profiles with observations (@sec-lrd).

**The Balmer decrement**, $L({\rm H\alpha})/L({\rm H\beta}) = 5.3$ (case B: 2.86), owes nothing to dust. Both lines are
optically thick, and each line's luminosity is set by its source function and the velocity field, not by
recombination statistics. Hβ is further weakened by absorption against the star: it has a trough down to 3 % of the
continuum at +160 km s$^{-1}$. The decrement depends on how the line power is counted. From the solution's own local
line powers it would be 8.9 instead of 5.3 (@sec-spec-energy). Either way it is far from case B **[computed]**.

**Redshifted Balmer absorption.** From Hβ upwards every Balmer line has an absorption trough at +160 to +180 km s$^{-1}$,
down to 3–8 % of the continuum, and from Hε up absorption wins over emission. The gas between us and the star falls away from us, so its absorption
is redshifted. Its source function in these lines is below the stellar intensity behind it. Redshifted absorption is
the kinematic signature of infall **[computed; interpretation]**.

**Paschen and Brackett** lines are strong: together $5.2\times10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$, 57 % of Hα. Their equivalent
widths are huge, Paα −3200 Å and Brα −7000 Å, because the stellar continuum is faint in the infrared. Paα/Hα = 0.19
**[computed]**.

**Lyα is weak**: 0.054 of Hα, against about 10 in case B for nebulae. Lyα is so optically thick that its photons
scatter until they are destroyed, mostly when the excited atom is photoionized from $n=2$. The higher Lyman lines are
in net absorption **[computed; interpretation]**.

## The energy in the lines {#sec-spec-energy}

The 23 emergent profiles carry $1.65\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$. The solution's own net line power (Sobolev escape,
summed over all 66 transitions of the model atom) is $1.12\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$. Line by line
(`julia/nlte_linepower.jl`) **[computed]**:

- For the strong emission lines, the emergent luminosity is 0.8–1.4 times the local net power: Hα 0.81, Lyα 0.81,
  Paα 0.87, Paβ to Brδ 0.94–1.32, Hβ 1.37.
- Most of the difference is in Hγ–Hθ. In the local balance they absorb $5.1\times10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$ of continuum. In the
  emergent spectrum they are close to neutral, $+0.2\times10^{42}$.
- The local balance counts all the light the gas absorbs, including light headed inwards to the star. The emergent
  profile counts only what is removed from the light that leaves. With temperatures held fixed, energy absorbed from
  the inward light goes nowhere, so the two need not agree **[interpretation]**.

So the strong lines are uncertain by 20–40 %, and the total line luminosity by about 50 %.

## What is not in this spectrum

- **Electron-scattering wings** of the lines, expected with $\tau_{\rm es} \approx 5$.
- **Helium** lines and non-LTE helium. The soft X-ray cut-off depends on it.
- **Metals**: none, since the model is at zero metallicity. So there is no Fe II, O I, Na D or Ca II.
- **Thermal balance** of the infall. It absorbs 8 % of $L$ at fixed temperature.
- **The infall beyond $30R$**, which is assumed out to $120R$.
- **Line opacity** in the star's own photosphere, which would reduce the far-UV excess (@sec-sm).
- **Asphericity**. Everything here is spherical: one viewing angle, no disc, no outflow.
